title: PROVISION OF MULTISOURCE ANALYTICAL ASSESSMENTS
description: The objective of this procurement procedure is the award of a multiple framework contract with reopening of competition with a maximum of 5 economic operators for the on-demand provision of analytical reports focusing on border security, cross-border crime, human smuggling, security and foreign policy in major countries of origin and transit to the EU member states and the Schengen associated states. These reports, known as Multisource Analytical Assessments (“MUSO”), will be based on open-sources information and geospatial analysis of earth observation data. They aim at supporting better-informed decision-making. The MUSO reports will use both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methodologies, including literature reviews, predictive data analytics, behavioural sciences and geospatial analysis. The reports will cover the specific needs of the European Union Satellite Centre ("SatCen") under the Service Level Agreement concluded by and between the SatCen and the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (“Frontex”).

title: Reference Mapping Products
description: This procurement procedure aims at the establishment of a multiple framework contract with reopening of competition with a maximum of seven selected tenderers, covering the production of reference mapping products that will facilitate the assessment of specific areas of interest in support of EU decision-making. The FWC will cover the production and delivery of five different types of products: Product 1 - Full Reference Mapping: High Resolution Vector Data (HRVD) products and provision of a background of geographical context, as well as a representation of a requested AOI, including hydrography, topography, land cover, infrastructure and population relevant data according to a Reference Mapping Data Dictionary (RMDD). The Full Reference Mapping encompasses 212 Feature Classes (Area: 105, Line: 43, Point: 64). Product 2 - Reduced Reference Mapping: HRVD products and provision of a background of geographical context, as well as a representation of a requested AOI, including lines of communications, land cover and other relevant data according to a subset of the RMDD. The Reduced Reference Mapping Product encompasses 117 Feature Classes (Area: 60, Line: 28, Point: 29). Product 3 - On-Demand Reference Mapping: HRVD products and provision of background of geographical context, as well as a representation of a requested AOI, with a limited set of Feature Classes which will be defined in each specific Product Request Form. Product 4 - Updated Reference Mapping: Updates of HRVD products that have already been produced, based on new extraction specifications as well as new imagery. Product 5 – Situational Mapping: HRVD product representing a requested AOI and a given set of limited and defined Feature Classes, compiled and delivered in a map book format. All of the aforementioned products will also require capabilities in processing Very High Resolution optical satellite imagery to create mapping-ready orthomosaics and open source information extraction to accurately complete the attribute tables of some features.

title: Provision of Multisource Analytical Assessments
description: The objective of this procurement procedure is the award of a multiple framework contract with reopening of competition for the on-demand provision of analytical reports focusing on border security, cross-border crime, human smuggling, security and foreign policy in major countries of origin and transit to the EU member states and the Schengen associated states. These reports, known as Multisource Analytical Assessments (“MUSO”), will be based on open-sources information and geospatial analysis of earth observation data. They aim at supporting better-informed decision-making. The MUSO reports will use both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methodologies, including literature reviews, predictive data analytics, behavioural sciences and geospatial analysis. The reports will cover the specific needs of the European Union Satellite Centre ("SatCen") under the Service Level Agreement concluded by and between the SatCen and the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (“Frontex”).

title: Provision of technical services for the AIDRA project demonstration on AI-enabled on-board data processing
description: The European Union Satellite Centre (SatCen) seeks to award a direct service contract to support the implementation of AIDRA (Artificial Intelligence In-orbit Data pRocessing Assessment), a cooperative initiative between the SatCen and the European Defence Agency (EDA). AIDRA is designed as a proof-of-concept to assess the feasibility, traceability, operational implications and governance conditions of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled On-Board Data Processing (OBDP) in support of Earth Observation (EO) and Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) workflows. The purpose of AIDRA is to generate independent, evidence-based insights into the maturity, risks and potential benefits of AI-OBDP for GEOINT, in support of EU objectives on technological readiness, operational effectiveness and secure information governance. The objective of the demonstration is to evaluate, under space-representative conditions, how AI-enabled on-board processing and tasking functions perform within an end-to-end EO data chain. The assessment focuses on technical behaviour, system performance and interaction with existing GEOINT workflow requirements. The initiative does not aim to deploy an operational capability, but to generate structured evidence to support institutional evaluation.

title: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft
description: Frontex is looking for EU Contractors to provide a fully-fledged service with manned fixed wing aircraft for aerial surveillance over sea which includes: a. aircraft; b. sufficient number of crew members (pilot, sensor operator, technician, etc.) in order to be able to deliver minimum 2 flight missions per day without any limitation; c. sufficient number of Liaison officer(s) in the assigned Operation Coordination Centre (Host MS ICC or Frontex HQ) during the entire deployment period, who will be working on the tasks related to the flight from 60 minutes before the moment of a take-off to 60 minutes following the landing; d. maintenance capability; e. data transmission capability via BRLOS (including near real time video streaming of the EO/IR) to the Operation Coordination Centre; f. logistical infrastructure and ground support (e.g. hangar, parking place of the aircraft, fuel, etc.); g. administrative responsibility (management of any permissions related to registration, certification, transportation, deployment, authorizations, insurances, permissions to fly, etc.) to deliver aerial surveillance over the external maritime border of the Host Country; h. the Contractor shall provide the collected data directly from the Asset to the designated Frontex Coordination Centre via BRLOS with a minimum uplink speed of 512 kbps. The Service which the Contractor shall provide under this FWC is based on mission flights where the Asset, following Frontex instructions, surveys the Area of Interest, included in the Service Deployment Area, searching for ‘objects of interest’ mandated by Frontex Regulation, and passing surveillance data and information to the Operational Coordination Centre designated by Frontex. Aircraft shall be able: - to reach the Area of Interest (surveillance area) located at a distance of more than 401NM from the Base Airport and; - deliver minimum 2.5 hours mission flight in the Area of Interest with the average speed as of approximately 150 knots, between 1000 feet and 6000 feet and return back to the base airport and; - to perform a total minimum of 6 hours of flight (excluding final reserve and contingency fuel) with 2 Frontex liaison officers on board in line with the requirements above, with the minimum mandatory Payload. These missions may also take place over Third Country (TC) waters, TC land territory, as well as to be operated from TC Base Airport. The aircraft has an approved life-raft drop capability (each life-raft has at least 10 PAX capacity, on board the total dropping capacity should secure enough life raft(s) for minimum 30 PAX) and in case of activation of life-raft drop the deployed aircraft can continue its mission flight (without an early landing) and after landing the second mission flight with full operational configuration (including life rafts) may take place within 60 minutes. Contracting Authority will consider as advantage the emergency broadcast system on the life raft 406 or 121.5 MHZ. Optionally, the aircraft can have the drop capability of life buoys able to broadcast minimum their position for at least 48 hours. The Contractor shall guarantee that the Asset is equipped with the following sensors: a. HD multi-sensor Electro-Optical/ Infrared camera for day and night operations; b. Automatic Identification System (AIS) receiver; c. Weather detection and avoidance system according to EASA and competent authorities’ prescriptions and certification requirements for the given type of Aircraft, in order to be able to perform all the type of flights requested by the prospective framework contract, following day and night IFR and VFR flight rules; d. Dedicated Maritime Surveillance Radar: minimum requirement to operate in X band and track minimum 500 simultaneous targets; e. Global navigation satellite system receiver; f. (Optional) Anti-jamming equipment in GNSS denied environment; g. Satellite phone. Duration of the future FWC: 2+2 years
